cards.claim: One atomic mass unit is exactly one-twelfth of the mass of one carbon-12 atom.
cards.quote: One atomic mass unit is defined as a mass exactly equal to one-twelfth of the mass of one carbon – 12 atom.

cards.claim: Molecular mass is the sum of the atomic masses of the elements in a molecule: each atomic mass times its number of atoms, added together.
cards.quote: Molecular mass is the sum of atomic masses of the elements present in a molecule. It is obtained by multiplying the atomic mass of each element by the number of its atoms and adding them together.

cards.claim: The average atomic mass of an element is computed by taking into account its isotopes and their relative abundances (per cent occurrence).
cards.quote: When we take into account the existence of these isotopes and their relative abundance (per cent occurrence), the average atomic mass of that element can be computed.

cards.claim: For ionic solids such as NaCl, which do not exist as single molecular entities, the formula mass is used instead of a molecular mass.
cards.quote: The formula, such as NaCl, is used to calculate the formula mass instead of molecular mass as in the solid state sodium chloride does not exist as a single entity.

cards.claim: NCERT Problem 1.1: the molecular mass of glucose C6H12O6 is 6(12.011 u) + 12(1.008 u) + 6(16.00 u) = 180.162 u.
The atomic masses listed in the periodic table are average atomic masses, not the mass of any single atom.
cards.quote: In the periodic table of elements, the atomic masses mentioned for different elements actually represent their average atomic masses.
